name: Abyssal Ghost Manta
desc: A shadow with nothing casting it, wider than the rupture it came through. It has never finished becoming a manta and shows no sign of intending to.

name: Abyssal Irisfin
desc: A thousand eyes open and close in no order and never all at once. Ratings who have gutted one report the pattern continues afterwards, on the inside.

name: Abyssal Gazer
desc: One eye the size of a fist, slotted crosswise. Ratings who hold the stare too long report it thrashing and suffocating, which it is not doing, and cannot.

name: Abyssal Necrophyte
desc: Comes up the line already decaying and stops at about half. The smell carries through a closed airlock, which no smell does.

name: Abyssal Eyestar
desc: Five arms, a hundred pupils, and no agreement between them about where the centre is. Holds together while watched and comes apart when it is not. Must be watched.

name: Abyssal Razorshrimp
desc: Flint-shelled and segmented past counting - several of those segments being perfect duplicates. The edges are sharper than the shape carrying them has any business supporting.

name: Abyssal Ridge Clam
desc: Opens along three hinges. Reality permits two.

name: Abyssal Shard Lobster
desc: Plated in something nearer slag than shell and cold enough to take skin off through a glove. It works its claws for a day after everything else in it has stopped.

name: Abyssal Aranea
desc: Neither fish nor spider and committed to both. The venom has resisted classification; medical advises against handling and the galley advises against everything else.

name: Abyssal Yellowback
desc: The one abyssal catch that looks almost ordinary. The yellow is not pigment and does not stay on the fish.

name: Abyssal Rockfish
desc: A void carried where the stomach should be. Prolonged observation eventually reveals the other side. Under no circumstances should you wave back.

name: Abyssal Nautilus
desc: A chambered shell wound inward, spiralling into itself past the point where there is anywhere left to go. Each chamber holds a little of the abyss it was pulled from and none of them drain.

name: Steel Pipechovies
desc: Arrives in bundles of five or six, each a straight length of dull steel with a mouth at the end. Whatever the ghost copied, it was not swimming at the time.

name: Roider Mudfish
desc: Bottom-feeder shape, bottom-feeder manner, in a medium with no bottom and no mud. Roider crews swear by them, which says more about roider crews than the fish.

name: Berylcuda
desc: Green-scaled and hard as its namesake mineral, with a barracuda's jaw grafted onto a food-stock body. Two patterns in one fish, and neither of them finished.

name: Coudplate Tetra
desc: Plated along the back in cloud-shaped scutes, armour against pressures hyperspace has never had. Collectors pay for the ones that came through symmetrical.

name: Tiger Sailfish
desc: Trails a dorsal banner longer than the fish, striped like something that meant to be seen. The banner keeps trailing for a moment after the fish has stopped.

name: Silver Slipstreamer
desc: Silver, and already at speed, holding a heading as though the slipstream it left were still running under it. One of the few that behaves as its shape suggests.

name: Green Bass
desc: Green, blunt, and obliging. A shape with nothing stronger to settle into settles into a bass, and some survey outfits have stopped recording them at all.

name: Jungle Snapper
desc: Small, deep-bodied and marked in reds and greens like something raised under a canopy. There is no canopy in hyperspace and the pattern does not appear to know it.

name: Blue Ochtogon Magifin
desc: Eight fins around a body plated in flat panels, too regular to be chance and lit along every seam. It is not built like an animal and does not move like one.

name: Blue Tang
desc: An untroubled blue that holds longer than most colours manage - the shape appears to suit whatever has assumed it. Reef stock, from reefs centuries under.

name: Soul Bream
desc: Broad, plain, and quiet, and the crews who bring them in will not say how the name came about. Something in a bream reads as occupied rather than alive.

name: Venomous Sailfish
desc: Sail-finned and patterned to warn rather than to hide, which turns out to be honest advertising. A week in the medbay for anyone who tests the claim.

name: Ole' Carp
desc: Grey, slow, and uninterested in resisting anything at all. Every ship of any age has one in the logs and not one crew remembers acquiring it.

name: Credfish
desc: Flat, hard-edged, and stamped along the flank with a figure the eye keeps trying to read as a denomination. Not legal tender in any port. This has stopped nobody.

name: Long Waller
desc: Two metres of whiskered patience, feeling along a riverbed that is not there and never was. Crews find it endearing or unbearable, with no ground in between.

name: Shimmerclam
desc: Shut on arrival and shut since, against every tool rated for the job. The shell runs through colours it carries no pigment for.

name: Corona Moth
desc: Broad-winged and ash-grey, wings angled to catch a light that does not reach this side. Near a star the angle is exact, and it holds through handling.

name: Common Crag Crab
desc: Comes up sideways and keeps going sideways across the deck until stopped. Ten legs, which is correct, and no comfort at all.

name: Volturnian Crab
desc: Blue through the shell rather than on it, and the closest thing to Volturn's own stock that hyperspace has ever handed over. Worth landing carefully.

name: Adolescent Pyrcrab
desc: Low, broad, and slow to commit to anything, which makes it one of the easier ones to have aboard. It runs warm to the touch, and warmer the longer it is held.

name: Adult Pyrcrab
desc: Full-grown, and hot enough to raise blisters through a work glove. Every rating describes a different fault in it, and each is sure the others are wrong.

name: Cutout
desc: A fish-shaped absence, visible where it overlaps something else and otherwise not. The tank shows the water it displaces. Feeding it is considered polite.

name: Eelcat
desc: Long, whiskered, and inclined to knot itself around whatever is nearest. The knots are not knots on inspection, but no better word has been offered.

name: Egg
desc: Hyperspace does not spawn, so this is a shape with no process behind it. It has never hatched, and standing orders are not to wait around and find out.

name: False Dawn
desc: A light in deep fabric that survey plots as a faint star with steady parallax. It is neither faint nor far, and it comes to the lamps. The cabin lighting runs a little behind itself while one is on the line.

name: Freight Clam
desc: A quarter-container in proportion and stencilling, hinged where a container is welded. The routing code checks out, and the destination port takes delivery without comment.

name: Bloody Damsel
desc: An orange so aggressive it reads as a warning light, and territorial about a territory that does not exist. Squares up to the drones the whole way in.

name: Goldfish
desc: Ornamental, inedible, and entirely without fight, turning up on ships whose crews have been thinking about home. Good luck to some crews and a wasted cast to the rest.

name: Bluefin Theta
desc: Rises for air in a medium that has none, over and over, at the surface of nothing at all. The blue along the fin is the only part of it that ever holds still.

name: Adolescent Razorspine
desc: Thin as a blade and hard as steel, yet moving as if made of flesh. Grips perfectly, throws steady, has claimed more than one life in ill-advised bets.

name: Hull Grazer
desc: Plated in overlapping armour the colour of old wrecks, worn bright at the edges. Specimens taken near debris fields carry fresh scratches on the inside of the plate.

name: Silver Razorspine
desc: Grown out, with a thick plate of patterned steel protecting a leathery underside. Heavy enough to deform gear rated well above it. The metal carries crude forge-marks.

name: Lunacyte
desc: Pale and unhurried, lit from within on a cycle that matches nothing aboard. Named by a crew that watched one for a full shift, and would not afterwards explain the name.

name: Poison Jelly
desc: Trails filaments far longer than the bell could support, and goes on trailing them after the bell has stopped. It stings for hours, and longer than that in the memory.

name: Aetherial Jelly
desc: Barely present and barely holding, a shape more suggested than built. Handled roughly it comes apart, and the pieces do not stay pieces for long.

name: Keystone
desc: Machined faces, clean tool marks, and a part number that appears in no catalogue anyone can reach. It swims poorly, which is to say it swims.

name: Lantern Jack
desc: An angler's build at hauler scale, and the lure is a distress beacon on the standard band. The signal is well-formed, decades stale, and stronger the closer the boat comes. Standing orders are to mark the position and keep the comms shut.

name: Mossy Bass
desc: Furred green along the back with something that is not moss, in a place with nothing for moss to grow on. Fights hard and briefly.

name: Largemouth Bass
desc: Big, blunt, obliging, and the most logged specimen in the Sector by a wide margin. Two together are never the same size, and never wrong in the same direction twice.

name: Larva
desc: A thing between shapes that stopped between them. Reality let it stand on the grounds that larvae are permitted to be unfinished.

name: Waterpillar
desc: Segmented and ringed, moving in a wave with nothing available to push against. A pattern common on land, which raises the question of where it came from.

name: Emmerling
desc: Named by the crew that recorded the first, and the name held for want of a competing suggestion. No template has been found for it, in Domain records or since.

name: Volturnian Lobster
desc: Blue-shelled and heavy through the claw, near enough the true Askonian article to fetch the true price. Near enough is doing the work, and the trade knows it.

name: Rock Lobster
desc: Grey, plain and gripping the line rather than being gripped by it. Good eating by the standards available out here, which is not a high bar.

name: Longliner
desc: At sensor range it returns a fishing boat: profile, mass and a working transponder. In the hold it is a third of that size and heavier than the readout at any of them. The transponder code has been landed before, in other systems, always the same.

name: Striped Mackerel
desc: Barred, quick and schooling with nothing to school with. The bars keep moving after the fish has stopped.

name: Marlin
desc: Long bill, long body, and a run that costs equipment. Bringing one in is generally the end of the work for that watch, one way or the other.

name: The Miscount
desc: The deck tally, the hold tally and the manifest disagree by one, and the one is always in the hold. Selling them does not bring the numbers together.

name: Mussel
desc: Clamped shut around an object that did not come through with it. Whatever it believes it is holding is not aboard.

name: Nav Bobber
desc: A marker buoy at one-third scale, holding station where nothing anchors it. The registration it blinks is well-formed and issued by nobody, and it keeps perfect time.

name: Deep Terror
desc: Eight arms, deep red, and a great deal better coordinated than the crew watching it. It gets into things, and it has never once been found where it was left.

name: Yellow King
desc: The markings resolve, given long enough, into a stage play set in yellow script. The first act is harmless. Crews who reach the second are relieved of duty and locked in the brig indefinitely.

name: Pacu Pacu
desc: Blunt, flat-toothed and disconcertingly human about the mouth. The teeth are the part of the pattern that came through cleanest.

name: Perch
desc: Striped, spiny and thoroughly ordinary. A relief, most nights.

name: Plume Remora
desc: Thin, blue-white, and always netted near the stern, keeping station off a drive nozzle the way a remora keeps station off a shark. No hull inspection has ever found one attached to anything.

name: Pomfret
desc: Silver, deep-bodied and easy to catch. Holds its shape better than most. Often a new crew's first catch and generally the only thing they remember about it.

name: Hyperprawn
desc: Translucent, thumb-length, and arriving by the hundred. The formations they hold while drifting cannot be looked at for long, and nobody has managed to say why.

name: Pufferfish
desc: Arrives slack and unimpressive, having concluded that the danger has passed. It has not.

name: Ballooner
desc: A pufferfish with its mind made up - inflated, spined, and declining to come back down. Reality permits the volume and is plainly unhappy about the source.

name: Deepwater Pufferfish
desc: Blue and already inflated on the way through the rupture, as though something down there startled it. Nothing did, as far as the instruments can say.

name: Silver Star
desc: Winged, silver, gliding on a medium with nothing to glide upon. It matches no record in any Domain database, and xeno-survey has declined to take an interest.

name: Gargantuan Waller
desc: A waller grown past all reason, heavy-headed and wrong about its own proportions. Takes two ratings and a winch, and reads as a catfish only until measured.

name: Nemo
desc: Banded orange and white and sealed in a bag of water nobody aboard put it in. The bag holds, and reads as standard plasteel on analysis.

name: Curious Damsel
desc: Small, bright, and inclined to follow machinery rather than flee it. Curiosity is not on the list of things these are supposed to be capable of.

name: Flarefin Koi
desc: Fins like a flare going off, trailing light that illuminates nothing around it. Ornamental stock from a garden nobody has placed, on a world nobody has named.

name: Undersea Bee
desc: Fist-sized, barely coherent, and arriving in swarms or not at all. The swarm behaves as one animal, which no single one of them is built to be.

name: Stinkfish
desc: The smell arrives first and outlasts the specimen by days. No compound has been isolated, which has not helped morale.

name: Blue Sea Tuna
desc: Big, blue, and built to cross an ocean in a place that has never held one. It makes the crossing anyway, at speed, in whatever direction it happened to be pointed.

name: The Quorum
desc: A school of some ten thousand silver bodies that arrives, turns and takes the hook as one animal, and is logged as one because it insists. However it is divided on deck, the tally comes to one.

name: Quorum Splinter
desc: A dozen silver bodies holding formation around nothing, cut out of a wall that did not close behind them. They keep the formation in the hold, and the tally counts them as one.

name: Rainbow Carp
desc: Ornamental, patterned in colours ship's screens cannot quite render. Worth more to a collector than to a galley.

name: Blind Crawler
desc: Eyeless, feeling its way along the bottom of a place with no bottom, and sounding a low note it needs water to make. It makes the note regardless, and keeps making it on the deck.

name: Red Snapper
desc: Deep red, sharp-toothed and a genuine fight. One of the few catches worth logging for its own sake.

name: Coach
desc: Small, silver, and absolutely everywhere. Named by a rating who found it funnier than it is, and the name went into the manifest before anyone could object.

name: Sulfur Diver
desc: Mottled yellow, reeking of sulphur, and inclined to hold position rather than run. It outlasts pursuit rather than outpacing it, which works more often than it should.

name: Storm Salmon
desc: Runs against a current that is not there, hard and in one direction, trailing charge the whole way. Nobody has established what it is running towards.

name: Sensor Ghost
desc: On the plot for hours before it is in the water: bearing steady, return clean, classification confident. The instruments log the catch a few seconds before the line moves.

name: Shad
desc: Thin silver schooling stock with no school to join. It arrives alone, and conducts itself throughout as though it were among thousands.

name: Silverback
desc: Heavy through the shoulder and silver along the spine, throwing itself clear of a surface that does not exist. A hazard to the drones and occasionally to the crew.

name: Skate
desc: Flat, winged, and gliding on nothing at all. It passes over the drones rather than through them, a distinction the machinery is not equipped to appreciate.

name: Skelleton
desc: Reality took the skeleton and declined the rest. Misspelled on the first survey sheet and every sheet since.

name: Slipstream Moray
desc: An eel long enough to file as a hazard to navigation, taken only where the fabric has nearly gone. Charted slipstreams in the area bend a few degrees toward wherever it is working, and the charts update to agree.

name: Spined Loach
desc: Small, whiskered, and armed under the eye with a spine that catches on everything. More trouble than it is worth, and the trade prices it accordingly.

name: Mind Flayer
desc: Nothing anyone has put in front of one has ever been eaten. Ratings quartered near one lose hours first, then names, then the ability to read. The specimen gains mass.

name: Crystal Aberration
desc: Faceted and rigid, lit from within in a colour that does not appear on the manifest. Whatever it is aberrating from, the record is clear that it is not going back.

name: Giant Squid
desc: Deep red, long-armed and inking freely, which is a problem when the ink does not stay where it lands. Bring a bucket, and something to put under the bucket.

name: Banana Star
desc: Five arms, yellow, curved, and jointed where arms are not jointed. Named by a rating who has since been quietly reassigned. Extremely venomous. Tastes like banana.

name: Crusty Star
desc: Blue, rough as old plating and entirely indifferent to being caught. Carries on doing whatever it was doing the whole way up.

name: Crystal Star
desc: Rigid, faceted, and ringing faintly whenever it is set down on anything hard. It appears in safety briefings, under the handling section, as the example.

name: Leafy Star
desc: Soft-armed, and regenerating anything taken off it faster than the available material accounts for. What the replacement is made of is a question nobody is funding.

name: Scraggly Star
desc: Thin-armed, uneven, and short one point - and never the same point twice. Reality appears to have made an accounting error here, and elected to let it stand.

name: Ice Tuna
desc: Heavy, cold through, frosted along the flank, and the best eating in the catalogue by a comfortable distance. Worth every bit of the gear it costs to bring one in.

name: Vulcan Cannonfish
desc: Blunt-nosed and barrel-bodied, built to the proportions of ordnance rather than of anything that ever swam. It assumed the shape nearest to hand, and found an autocannon.

name: Weathervane
desc: Narrow, rigid, and pointed the same way regardless of current, tank or handling. Charted against survey data the heading resolves to the nearest rupture. Nobody consults it.

name: Amberjack
desc: Fast, yellow along the tail and a long fight for its size. Sought by crews who have grown tired of bass.
